my first paper

Author

Kevin Hu

Abstract:This paper is a simple introduction to the two-stage least squares (TSLS) method, which is used to estimate the parameters of a model when there are endogenous variables. The paper provides an overview of the TSLS method, including its assumptions and limitations, and discusses its applications in various fields such as economics, finance, and social sciences. The paper also presents a case study using real-world data to illustrate the application of the TSLS method and its advantages over traditional ordinary least squares (OLS) regression.

3.1 preparation

Code 
```{r}
# filter mroz data set: women with positive wage and in labor force
moroz_spl <- mroz %>%
  filter(wage>0, inlf==1) %>%
  select(wage, educ, exper, expersq, fatheduc, motheduc, huseduc)
```

3.4 TSLS

We will use three IVs: motheduc, fatheduc, huseudc

the stage 1 model:

\[ educ = \gamma_0 +\gamma_1 exper + \gamma_1 expersqr +\theta_1 motheduc + \theta_2 fatheduc + \theta_3 huseduc + v_i \]

lm.hus <- lm(formula = model_hus, data = mroz)

summary(lm.hus)

3.6 Cragg-F test

Code 
```{r}
# filter samples
mroz1 <- wooldridge::mroz %>%
  filter(wage>0, inlf==1)
# set parameters
N <- nrow(mroz1)
G <- 2 
B <- 2
L <- 2 
# for endogenous variables
x1 <- resid(lm( mtr ~ kidslt6 + nwifeinc, data = mroz1))
x2 <- resid(lm( educ ~ kidslt6 + nwifeinc, data = mroz1))
# for instruments
z1 <-resid(lm(motheduc ~ kidslt6 + nwifeinc, data = mroz1))
z2 <-resid(lm(fatheduc ~ kidslt6 + nwifeinc, data=mroz1))
# column bind
X <- cbind(x1,x2)
Y <- cbind(z1,z2)
# calculate Canonical correlation
rB <- min(cancor(X,Y)$cor)
# obtain the F statistics
CraggDonaldF <- ((N-G-L)/L)/((1-rB^2)/rB^2)
```
